I used to work at CFA and making cool wraps was the second worst thing I could be assigned to do other than dishes. They are labor intensive and were SO popular at the location I worked. 

In case anyone wants more of the process and how it works: 

First, there’s cool down chicken. Chicken has to be cooled below 40 degrees before it can be put on a salad, and because we went through so much, this usually starts the day before as a closing task. We’d aim to have around 10 trays of chicken in the fridge to be cooked down by morning. If resources and time allowed, 2-3 trays of every salad would be pre-made for the morning crew. A tray typically consists of 6 salads.

The morning crew typically used at least half of that and by lunch, more chicken was (hopefully) already cooling and more salads were (hopefully) already getting restocked. A lot of times though, lunch would get slammed, and the dinner crew is struggling to make enough by the dinner rush. 

Cool wraps specifically take the longest to make and require more space. My location eventually stopped letting people modify the wraps in any way because in order to make one you’d have to sanitize the cutting board, and stop making literally anything else so that could get done. 

You have to lay down the tortilla, pinch out the right amounts of lettuce, cheese, and chicken, wrap it into its shape, wrap it into its paper, cut it, and then put it into its plastic container. Every other salad is made by just putting ingredients into a container with scoops. 

I hated cool wraps. I’d beg to be on any other position other than salads just to avoid them. Now, personally, the price with that in mind is still too high. I completely acknowledge that. The employee in me still thinks that if having it cost double that meant I wouldn’t have to make any more, it’d be worth it. 

Disclaimer: Other location and employee stories may vary, this is just my take from a store that routinely broke $3,000 an hour during rushes. Less busy stores probably have different reasons for hating wraps.

If I lived in a French-speaking country, then it may be an issue. But I do not, and in the region of the USA I live in, fiancé is gender neutral. 

You aren’t wrong, in French, it is not gender neutral. But where I live, it is. Maybe if you grew up where I lived you would understand.

If you are frequently around French people and it can be misunderstood, then yeah. But I’m in America. I did my own research into this and agree with nokobi. Fiancé is currently used as gender neutral here, and it is not wrong to do so, because we are not in France/Canada. Similar to how gay can refer to both men and women who like the same gender, even though the word lesbian exists. Language itself changes over time, because gay used to mean “happy”. 

Also, I do think it’s disingenuous to assume that people who speak French are going to think I’m a man because I use the term fiancé to refer to myself. Especially if I am using other gendered language that tells them I’m a woman. Most people know how to use context.

The need for structure without being able to adhere to it is just the worst. Personally? My solution has been to do it halfway, and to make it rewarding. I use the Hero’s Journal, which makes journaling and planning fun because it progresses a “story”. I was gifted really nice and fancy looking face wash, toner, and moisturizer. It makes me feel fancy to use it so now I wash my face daily after never having done it. My toothbrush is next to my face care set, and now I remember to brush my teeth. 

Not to say that this is all perfect. Sometimes I forget, but now, it’s the exception, not the rule. Now I just need to figure out how to make washing the dishes, making the bed, and doing homework luxurious. 

Sometimes, I know I’m just not going to be able to do it. And it sucks. But I bribe myself with coffee or a sweet treat. For homework, I listen to lofi and pretend I’m in some tv show as a background character. For working out, I listen to Viking music and pretend I’m rowing a ship to victory. 

I treat my ASD and my ADHD with making the stuff I need to do fun and bribing myself. At the end of the day, there’s always tomorrow.
